newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hamas calls for "total confrontations" with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hamas calls for "total confrontations" with Israel.

text.p: The Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas on Thursday urged Palestinians to head to "total confrontations" with Israeli forces and settlers after Friday prayers in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"Hamas Movement calls our heroic people to come out after Friday prayers tomorrow in marches and total confrontations against the forces of the Zionist occupation and its herds of settlers," the militant group said in a statement.

"The popular and military Palestinian resistance must remain the spearhead in confronting the Zionist designs and projects, until victory and liberation," added the statement, faxed to an international news agency in Beirut.
Hamas claimed responsibility for suicide bombings which killed 59 people in Israel in February and March, but since then its activists have held their fire.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat launched a crackdown against Hamas after the bombings, detaining many of its militants and taking a heavy toll on the movement.

Hamas' call came a day after a two-day Israeli-Palestinian summit at the White House convened by U.S. President Bill Clinton to discuss ways to end recent violence that has killed 73 Arabs and Jews in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank.

The violence -- the worst Israeli-Palestinian fighting since they signed a September 1993 peace deal -- was touched off by Israel's opening of an entrance to an archaeological tunnel in Jerusalem which offended Palestinian religious sensitivities because it runs near Moslem holy places.

Hamas said its call was "to express the continuation of the Aqsa intifada as long the threat to the holy Aqsa mosque remains by keeping the sinister tunnel open and so long as the crimes of Judaisation and settlement continue."

It dismissed the Washington summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein as another failure for Arafat "even in partial issues like closing the new Zionist tunnel under the Aqsa or the redeployment of enemy forces in Hebron."

Netanyahu, who has accused Arafat of having incited last week's violence, gave no commitment to close the tunnel nor a target date for the partial pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron agreed by the previous Labour-led government.
The West Bank and Gaza were quiet on Thursday but Israelis and Palestinians voiced doubts the calm would continue.
Israeli tanks remained in position around Palestinian towns ahead of U.S.-brokered talks due to start on Sunday in Gaza on Israel's long-delayed troop redeployment from Hebron.
Hamas representative in Lebanon, Mustapha Liddawi, told Reuters the Palestinian Authority on Wednesday asked all opposition factions, including Hamas, to practise restraint.
He said Palestinian police set up checkpoints on the edge of the so-called Green Line seperating them from Israeli forces and were barring any Palestinian gatherings facing the Israelis.

"Our people are determined to confront the Zionist forces deployed around the cities with childrens' stones, young men's chests, and mothers' supplications even if Arafat has pledged to repress the intifada," Hamas said.
"The strugglers of our people will continue to pursue every Zionist in the land of Palestine despite Arafat's committments to the Zionists and Americans," the statement added.
